lines: In a solo episode, Alex Kantrowitz argues that reports of Jensen Huang's affair with a woman US intelligence reportedly links to Chinese intelligence are a national-security problem for Nvidia, not just a personal scandal.
He frames Huang as a near-irreplaceable leader, so any hit to his standing threatens Nvidia's stability, and raises the risk that sensitive communications or chip strategy may have been exposed.

Kantrowitz says the episode undercuts Huang's credibility as the leading voice against US export controls on AI chips, and lands just as a shift in congressional control sets up hearings on AI and national security.
He notes rivals such as Google are using the uncertainty to pitch TPUs as an alternative, especially to government and heavily regulated customers.
Still, he expects Huang to keep his job, arguing the industry's dependence on Nvidia and the momentum of the AI build-out shield it from the usual corporate consequences.
title: Jensen and The Honeypot
